messages:
Maria (Marketing): heads up — SRE flagged a partial degradation in EU West at 04:12 UTC. latency spikes for embeddings & streaming. can we pick status wording + customer email timing?
Charles (SRE): confirmed. some requests are 5-7x latency, errors ~1.4%. working on fallback route to other region. ETA for mitigation 45–90m. will update root status.
Maria (Marketing): ok — want to align public status + an outbound note for customers on dedicated plans. aim to post status now and an email at the 30m mark if impact persists. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Ajay (Support): support queue seeing tickets from EU customers asking if data is affected. must have clear customer-facing line about data integrity.
Lena (Comms): agree on data line. propose: "No customer data was accessed or lost. This is a performance degradation affecting request latency and some timeouts." short and blunt.
Tom (Product): +1. Also recommend callout for customers using region-pinned Dedicated: they'll see increased latency; advise temporary routing to global endpoints.
Charles (SRE): proposed status page copy (short):
```
Investigating — Partial latency degradation in EU West affecting embeddings and streaming responses. Service is degraded for a subset of traffic; no data loss reported. Engineers are routing traffic and working on a mitigation. Next update in 30 minutes.
```
Maria (Marketing): that reads well. need a shorter banner for the status page list view (1 line).
Lena (Comms): banner suggestion: "Partial degradation in EU West — working on mitigation; no data loss."
Ajay (Support): for the email subject line options:
- "Service update: EU West latency issue — we're on it"
- "Redwood: temporary performance issue in EU West"
Pick one and we'll send to affected accounts if outage >30m.
Maria (Marketing): pick the first one. Draft email body (short) below — can you check tone?
```
Subject: Service update: EU West latency issue — we're on it
Hi —
We detected a performance issue impacting requests served from our EU West region. Engineers are routing traffic and working on a mitigation. There is no indication of data loss. We will provide another update in 30 minutes or when we have a clear resolution.
If you rely on region-pinned Dedicated capacity and need help routing traffic, reply to this message and Support will assist.
— The Redwood Team
```
Lena (Comms): tone is good — keep it plain, no defensive language. add a line with links: status.redwood.com/incident/1855 and support.redwood.com.
Maria (Marketing): timeline agreement: post status now (Charles), send first email at 30m if still degraded, send final email when resolved. social posts only after restored with root cause in follow-up.
Charles (SRE): posted status and created incident page id 1855. incident-bot: "Incident 1855 created — EU West latency degradation — severity: Sev2"
incident-bot: Incident 1855 created — EU West latency degradation — severity: Sev2
Ajay (Support): prepping canned responses for tickets. will include the subject and the status link.
Tom (Product): quick question — should we trigger auto-reroute for Dedicated customers or wait for manual opt-in? ops: what risks?
Charles (SRE): auto-reroute could help but risk of cross-region bandwidth. for now manually advise customers; we can enable auto-reroute if impact grows past 5% error or 60m.
Maria (Marketing): ok we'll include that guidance in the email: 'Support can help enable temporary routing to alternate regions.'
Lena (Comms): final check — change "mitigation" to "workaround" in the banner? I prefer 'mitigation' for status page.
Maria (Marketing): leave as mitigation. I'll queue the email template in Helpdesk and mark recipients as 'affected by EU West region'. Ajay — please confirm recipient list.
Ajay (Support): will run query and confirm within 10m.
Charles (SRE): next update in 30m or earlier if resolved. posting updates on incident page as progress is made.
Maria (Marketing): thanks everyone — I'll stand by for the 30m check and to approve the send. :thumbsup:
